cards.front: Recall a key point about Akhirah: Life After Death
cards.back: Muslims believe that physical death is not the end — there is an afterlife (akhirah). After death, the soul is questioned in the grave by Munkar and Nakir, and on the Day of Judgement (Yawm al-Din), all people will be resurrected and judged by Allah.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Akhirah: Life After Death
cards.back: Belief in akhirah is one of the Six Articles of Faith. Without it, the whole Islamic moral framework would collapse — there would be no ultimate justice and no reason to follow Allah's commands if this life is all there is.

cards.front: What should you know about uk context?
cards.back: The Islamic funeral ritual reflects belief in akhirah: the body is washed, wrapped in a simple white shroud and buried facing Makkah as quickly as possible. Mourners recite the Shahadah and pray for the deceased’s forgiveness. In the UK, Muslim burials must comply with both Islamic law (which requires burial, not cremation) and UK cemetery regulations.

cards.front: What should you know about uk context?
cards.back: The Prophet said: “The one who has the least punishment in Hell will have two shoes of fire, and his brain will boil because of them” (Sahih Bukhari). Even the least punishment is severe, which motivates Muslims to avoid sin and seek Allah’s forgiveness through prayer, charity and good deeds.

cards.front: What should you know about uk context?
cards.back: In 2023, Birmingham City Council approved a new Muslim burial section at Brandwood End Cemetery, reflecting the growing need for Islamic burial facilities in the city, which has one of the largest Muslim populations in the UK outside London.

Students often confuse Sunni and Shi'a beliefs about predestination. Wrong: "All Muslims believe everything is predestined and humans have no free will." Correct: "Most Muslims believe God has foreknowledge but humans have free will to choose; the balance between predestination and free will is understood differently across traditions."
